[quote=koranvistan;61583486]Elena, with a lidded tray of various pastries under her arm, opened the door to the Markov House. The frontroom was small, and had a coat rack, boot tray, and some family photos. One in particular stood out- a tall, spindly guy next to a lady who could be Elena with darker hair, both gazing at a newborn child. Elena noticed Cecilia staring and smiled, [i]"The only time you'll see my father smile is at a baby, or a young animal. And my mama.. we'll,  you'll see where I get it from."[/i] She gestured to her face, and leaned in to plant a peck on her partners cheek. She turned and stepped out of the frontroom, into what looked like a refinished kitchen/dining room.

[i]"Mama!"[/i] she called, [i]"Mama the impossible has been done!"[/i]

From the other side of the house, the sound of hurried footsteps moved down the stairs and quickly clacked along the ground. And thankfully she had set down the tray- for the Missile (Erwin, the family dog) had taken her down. A lady followed into the room, observing the dog and the girl on the floor. She looked to Veronika, [i]"This German girl, is she yours? She can't be mine!"[/i]

Veronika laughed, [i]"Well I didn't bring the dog here!"

"Mama!"[/i] Elena struggled from the ground, victim to Rottweiler affections, [i]"You can't go calling me a dog in front of my girlfriend!"[/i] she laughed and pulled her mom into a hug. [i]"and Pa?"[/i]

[i]"Oh he's at work, you know how he is."

"I'll have to take his job at this rate."

"I'll have to find him another. Girlfriend?"[/i]
Elena nodded and grabbed Cecilias hand, introducing the two.
[i]"Cecilia, this is my mother, Marniy,"[/i][/quote]
Cecilia watched the scene of chaos unfold before her and couldn't help but let a smile tug at her lips. Her gaze followed the dog as it appeared and she gasped as he tackled Elena before lightly laughing at the situation.

She calmed herself a little as she approached Elena's mother. With a smile, she spoke. [i]"It's very nice to meet you, [b]Pani Markov.[/b]" She outstretched her hand for a handshake.

[b]The Committee[/b]

The room of the committee, which had been rented out via cash, for fear of raising suspicions, was located in a rather old, rather grimy, and rather unsuitable office building that had been built in the 1970s, and clearly not renovated ever since.

Lambeau entered the room first, his cane in hand like a baton, his coat meticulously placed upon his shoulders, and his powdered wig perched atop his head like a crown. Peering around the room at the wooden tables that were arranged in a U shape, he moved and sat down, then entered Mr. Z and Mr. Meternisse, dressed in equally fine clothing, though Meternisse was more proletarian in his form, his wig being much simpler.

They sat down, and after greeting each other with nods, Lambeau spoke, Gentlemen, what are our aims? he asked in a calm tone.

To write a petition of grievances, replied Meternisse.
Correct, thank youeuh is Mrs. Landingham here? he asked, looking around for the aforementioned lady, who was a personal friend of Meternisse. 

Ah, sadly, she called me today to inform me she has la grippe, replied Meternisse with a frown.

Well then, replied Lambeau with a nod, We shall then have to have Mr. Z take our notes, he smiled at the frowning Montfleurois man, who rolled his eyes and pulled out a notepad and pen from a bag he had brought with him. 

Hear hear, he replied with a sigh.

Now, this document is to address the grievaqnces we have with the government of Rosenmarkke, so what have we? asked Lambeau, looking at the two other men.

Undemocratic processes, elections fraud, began Meternisse, listing off the crimes on his fingers.

Yes! And all provable, replied Lambeau.

This war that Rosenmarkke entered, would you be able to claim the government egged on the Wuloosyans? asked Mr. Z.

Perhaps, the sequence of events hasnt yet been fully agreed upon, replied Lambeau.

So right now we have elections fraud, and the prevention of democracy, tapped Mr. Z as he frowned and scratched his wig, What else? 

International misbehaviour, replied Meternisse hesitantly.

Hah, chortled Mr. Z, That is every nation sir, 

He is right, Meternisse, that literally is every nation, I would change that to, crimes against the people through actions which deprive them of their liberty, such as fraudulent elections, the control of information contrary to the government and the limitation of free speech, the construction of prison camps for political dissidents, began Lambeau, his tone rising excitedly.

Yes, yes, go on, replied Mr. Z, scribbling down notes faster.

Impeding upon workers rights through the forced unification of all workers unions under government oversight! declared Meternisse, jumping up excitedly and slamming his cane onto the table.

Please Meternisse, d-mn you, sit down, declared Lambeau with a nod of his head and wave of his hand, Acting for a school child landssake,

Meternisse apologised and the meeting continued.

The gentlemen made conversation about the wording and the exact nature of the petition; they agreed that it would be ignored most likely, but would gain traction among the people, which, according to Meternisse, mattered more than getting the attention of the government.

As the meeting concluded, the decision was to meet a month later to discuss the actual first draft of the petition, in the meantime theyd inform the president of the affairs of that meeting.

[b]June 5, 2028: Whispers and Papers[/b]

Since the end of the war between Wuloosya and Rosenmarkke, the nation of Rosenmarkke had been quietly attempting to rebuild itself; however, the war had torn open a gaping wound in the strict security state system that had been constructed. Contrary to popular promises under Polenne Strømm, no election was held in April to remake the legislature, indeed Strømm had been killed in March, and her brother Haakon had taken power by decree of the emergency Council of 99 within five days of her death and funeral. 

While the state security apparatus, the SCSID, had initially maintained the environment of propaganda and glory that had been fostered by Polenne, the loss of the Rosenmarkket navy and the massive failures of the air defense and armed forces in the war had exposed how outdated, paper-thin, and weak the government actually was at properly defending its citizens, rather preferring to maintain the ideals of the Eternal Revolution and the preservation of the state, rather than focus on the needs of the people. 

These were the words in the briefing given to King Henri XVII of Montfleur, the poorer, more populous neighbour of Rosenmarkke, neutral since the 30s and proud of it. Upon receiving word of these affairs, he sat down at a marble-topped table and stared out towards the gardens of the palace of Valcur. The advisors waited nervously to hear what would be reported to them by the king.

The Rosenmarkket regime, intoned the king, Is coming to a close, he continued, And we are here to witness it, 

There was another pause, another length of silence, before he turned to one of the advisers, a Mssr. Villiarde DuPont and said, I have received word, from other sources, that there is a small movement in both countries, mine and Rosenmarkke, that champions the cause of re-unificationmy question isdo we take them serious Villiarde?

Villiarde bowed politely and replied, Your majesty, I believe that taking these people seriously, would destabilise the nation greatly, it is a fools errand to attempt re-unification, Rosenmarkke would object, 

But, intoned the king, lifting his finger, But, there are reports that the Council of 99, the emergency council they assembled, has not been dismissed, even though the emergency is gone, so why do it then?

Villiarde bowed, Our intelligence says that they are still attempting to find those loyal to Strømm in order to build a new SCSID, her brother, Haakon, has been slow at it, 

The king pursed his lips and nodded, And there have been protests, right? 

Yes, replied Villiarde.
What are the metrics here on re-unification? asked the king.

We do not have them yetthe reunification crowd is the usual, nobility, nationalists, historical nostalgists, 

What would it take to get a vote on this? asked the King.

Probably the Rosenmarkket side conceding or requesting, replied Villiarde.

The king sighed, Lets get some reports running on this, seek out some supporters, I heard that Sallach or some voices in Sallach support the matter, and they probably could sway some of our people, also, I want to get SummitONE on the phone to see what they might be able to pull, and make sure the president knows of this,

Villiarde nodded, and the two other aids also nodded, bowing before leaving the room. The makings of history had begun.

[b]Canon-Based Review of the Stabilization of the Bununaq and Yakutia Regions[/b]

Since Minhokae's annexation of Bununaq and Yakutia, the King, at the request of the Prime Minister and Minister of Defense, had ordered the partial mobilization of the reserves as a way to compensate for leveraging control over more land area. Until the population in those regions was calmed of any civil unrest, violent altercations with the military present there, or any form of violent resistance to the new government, soldiers of Minhokaen ethnicity had to be present before conscription was introduced there.

On the document that the Bunun and Yakut tribesmen had signed confirming their annexation into The Kingdom of Minhokae, there were a few instances where autonomy was mentioned, after the initial 30-120 days of stabilization and control and the beginning of administrative integration with autonomy. It was interpreted that Minhoakaen law was to be incorporated, with full incorporation expected by the 365 day deadline.

Due to this, conscription was to be extended to the newly-annexed regions as well. This would allow for the reserves to be able to go back to their reserve state and to return home, and for more prosperity and peace to be brought to the regions. All male citizens aged 18 and higher were required to go to their local Military Enlistment Office and register. There, the names of all of the males registered, and that confirmed their citizenship. They would undergo interviews to confirm all of the members of their immediate family, including grandparents, and the military would go to their places of residence and confirm their identities.

Once that process was finished, all males who were in the military, as well as their immediate family members, were declared citizens of The Kingdom of Minhokae. They would swear an oath of allegiance to the King, confirm who they say they are, and would be given passports and citizenship/documentation papers within a few days, weeks, or months, depending on the work load of the Ministry of Justice. Temporary IDs were issued on the spot.

From there, all males aged 19 were expected to return to their local Military Enlistment Office and undergo a physical and mental examination to confirm their ability to serve in the Armed Forces, and had their role in the Army determined by a higher military authority. They served for 18 months, and, upon their completion of their time as conscripted soldiers, were transferred to the reserves, where they would stay until they turned 50 years old. Males who refused to go to their local Military Enlistment Office during these times were subject to high fines and imprisonment.

They would be ineligible for any sort of benefits from the state, declared illegal, and their families were interrogated to make sure that they were loyal to the King and to Minhokae. If they were found to be loyal, the family would be granted citizenship after a period of time of routine visits from military officers. Until then, they would be declared legal residents of Minhokae, but not citizens. They would be granted citizenship after the completion of the period of time which included visits from military officers.

The families of the males of who refused to present themselves to a Military Enlistment Office were interrogated to make sure that they were loyal to the King and the Kingdom of Minhokae, and if they were not, they would be declared stateless and issued stateless IDs, but still had the rights to live in the region. However, if a family opposed the decision of a male from their family to not serve in the military and were loyal to the King and to the Kingdom of Minhokae, they would be subject to frequent visits, declared legal residents of Minhokae, and citizens at the designated time.

If individual family members supported decisions outside of their families, the same situations would occur, depending on the opinion. If a family opposed the decision of the male who decided to serve in the military, they were declared stateless and issued stateless IDs. With this, Minhokae had a high number of males who pledged allegiance to the King and to the Kingdom of Minhokae, securing their support and that of their families.

Minhokae garnered much support from the population, because this gave them the benefits of being citizens of the Kingdom of Minhokae as well as autonomy rights, as long as they pledged allegiance to the King and to the Kingdom of Minhokae. With the absence of large amounts of men aged 18-35, the threat of any stronger resistance to Minhokae's authority was weakened, and thus allowed Minhokae to proceed with the phases of annexation as planned. Minhokae also made and kept its promise to keep traditional sites, buildings, and structures intact and protected by national law, and invested over 1% of its GDP in the process. 0.4% of the GDP (4,000,000,000) was dedicated to direct family income support for the full 365 day annexation timeline so that they could get on their feet and ready for a new society before they got settled themselves (approximately 28,880 per family). 0.6% of its GDP (6,000,000,000) was dedicated towards infrastructure support and construction in those regions. 30% of this (1,800,000,000) was dedicated to roads, bridges, tunnels, rail spurs, railroads, and connections in general to Minhokae's core territory. 20% (1,200,000,000) was dedicated to power plants, grids, fuel depots, and dual-use military logistics hubs. 15% (900,000,000) was dedicated to water systems, flood control, and basic housing upgrades. Another 15% was dedicated to hospitals, clinics, schools, and rehab centers, specially dedicated to supporting conscript and reserve families. 10% (600,000,000) was dedicated to broadband, ID systems, and tax and registration registries. Another 10% was given to military bases, training grounds, reserve depots, and dual-use airfields. [/spoiler]

Three days after Faris had staged the purge, all the dissenters had been tried. Under the charges of high treason and conspiracy to murder the leader of Hydronia, they were sentenced to death. Evidence was fabricated, and in many instances those who were on trial confessed falsely to save their own lives while damning a few more. The primary evidence to the trials was the statement made by Omar ibn Abdullah, who was now nowhere to be found.

Gunshots rang out through the streets. Crowds eyed the executions, hatred in their gazes for those who came together to kill the man of the people. Blood ran down cold pavement sidewalks.

In groups of three, they were executed. The shootings began at noon, and continued through the setting of the sun.

Faris stood on the balcony of the presidential palace, overlooking the executions that were happening around him. It was vivid beyond vividity, and yet he felt he was asleep. He had to be dreaming. He nearly pinched himself to wake up from this vision.

By the end of the day, all of the traitors were executed. Faris rested in his office, not glad that this had taken place but now calmer knowing that his position was cemented. The traitors were those that had the highest capacity to oppose him, and now there were none; if there were any less he was certain that they would remain quiet now that he had set a new precedent.

With the last of the light he saw as the bodies were collected and hauled into one large truck with the top of the container removed so that there would be more space. There were bodies upon bodies, and limbs poked out from the mass propped up only by the limbs of others. He knew that the destination was an unmarked mass grave somewhere off in some unknown area. Late at night, Faris remained in his suit and tie, unable think about going to bed. He felt some undue fear grip his heart, and he felt himself unable to rest. Perhaps it was anxiety at watching the executions, or perhaps his conscience from murdering his own brother catching up to him, but it was something that needed to be suppressed. He left his office and turned left to use a small restroom; there were others that were larger, but this small restroom was closest and he knew himself in need of quick respite.

Faris kept the lights off. He turned on the sink and began to wet his face with cool water, which ran down to his neck and dried upon reaching his shirt. Faris looked slightly deeper into the mirror which he had only looked at in passing. The darkness made it difficult to distinguish any features while he stood at a normal distance. Even then, it appeared as though there was some sort of abnormality; it was not that he could not make out the details of his face due to the darkness, but rather that there was a black shroud covering him. It unsettled him deeply.

A crack appeared on the mirror. Faris took a step away; his mind was screaming at him to move, yet his body was paralyzed with fear. Now the black shroud had dissolved, and what he saw unnerved him more: it was his own face, sneering at him. He was certain that this was not the expression on his own.

Suddenly the mirror shattered outwards and an arm black as coal reached out to him and grabbed him by the neck. It tightened its grasp, intending to kill him, and Faris quickly reacted by reaching for the knife at his side and bringing it down on the limb, cutting himself free. The rest of the limb retreated, but three more appeared and shot forth towards him.

Faris jumped back, coughing and clawing the still tight hand away from his throat. A creature from the depths of hell began to crawl out. One hundred arms reached through the small opening, clawing at anything they could reach to pull themselves through.

[i]"Guards!"[/i] Faris staggered backwards. He overcame the paralysis of fear that had taken hold of him and turned to open the door. At the moment he turned the handle he heard the sound of that horrid creature stumble and fall onto the ground with its many limbs already starting to reorient it to chase after him. He did not wait to look back; Faris sprinted down the hall.

The creature was behind him, and galloped with many legs and arms. Its myriad voices called out to him, stumbling upon each other, some mocking him and others weeping and others yet babbling incoherently as children. On the corridors were hands and shadows of hands reaching out to him, some colored as coal or tar and others with varying levels of decay, many with missing flesh and raw muscle exposed and others stripped to the bones and sinews.

Faris could only keep running. He sprinted straight down the corridor, and he could hear the creature gaining on him. He turned right, intending to get to his office, and he could hear the demon go past the turn with its many limbs trying to grab at the carpeted floor and slipping under the inertia. He looked back and saw the hands of the creature pulling itself around the corner of the wall; the mass of flesh reared its ugly heads with faces that were vaguely familiar to him.

He was closing in on his office door. He knew that if he could just lock himself in there, the strong wooden door would block out the devil that chased him. There was enough distance between him and the creature for him to feel confident he could make it, and when he finally reached his office he slammed the large door behind him and locked it. There was a strong impact, and the walls shook with force. The doorknob rattled wildly and the pounding of many fists against the door filled the office room. Faris scrambled to his desk, where he kept a revolver; he had no time to make sure that it was fully loaded, but rather kept it pointed at the door.

The pounding ceased, and the cacophony of voices slowly quieted and fell silent. Faris believed that the creature had left him, when suddenly the sound of shattering glass pierced the air behind him as thousands of mirror shards fell broken upon the floor. Faris whipped around, and once more the entanglement of arms and flesh had appeared. He had locked himself in the room with the creature.

The devil charged him, and he aimed and fired twice in quick succession. It did not stop the hurling mass from coming down upon him, and in the final moments he squeezed his eyes tight and fired once more.

For a few seconds there was silence and blackness. He squeezed the trigger again and again only to be met with the soft click of the revolver each time. He opened his eyes.

There was nothing there.

There were the sounds of footsteps, and suddenly frantic knocking on the large wooden door. [i]"President Al-Mansoori! Is everything alright? We heard you call for us and run into here, and sounds of gunfire!"[/i]

The knocking against the door ceased for a moment as the handle tried to turn, and then the knocking resumed. Faris took a moment to analyze the situation: he was unharmed, and the devil that had tormented him was gone.

He went to open the door. [i]"I am alright. Please, leave me be."[/i]

The guards left. He looked back into his office and saw that the mirror was intact. However, he could feel the cuts on his own face from where the bathroom mirror shards had cut him, and he tasted the slightest hint of blood.
